case.title: st.multiselect loses the selection when I click another button
case.body:
Every time I click any button, the items picked in my multiselect are cleared.

```python
import streamlit as st

items = load_items()
picked = st.multiselect("Items", list(items))
if st.button("Refresh"):
    st.write(picked)
```

- Streamlit version: 1.52.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Browser: Firefox
case.author: reporter

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: No page reload, it happens on normal clicks. load_items() returns a set, so the options come in a different order each time.

evidence.title: Understanding widget behavior
evidence.snippet: A widget's identity depends on the arguments passed to the widget command. If no key is provided, changing a widget's label, min value, max value, default value, placeholder text, or help text will cause it to reset.
evidence.relation: Explains why a widget without a key can reset when its parameters change between reruns.

evidence.title: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun
evidence.snippet: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun
evidence.relation: Same widget and symptom (selection dropped on rerun); open, confirmed bug.

evidence.title: Add statefulness to apps
evidence.snippet: For each browser tab that connects to the Streamlit server, a new session is created.
evidence.relation: State is per session; a reload or a new tab starts a new, empty session.

evidence.title: Understanding widget behavior
evidence.snippet: If you don't call a widget command in a script run, Streamlit will delete the widget's information, including its key-value pair in Session State.
evidence.relation: A keyed widget that is skipped in one run loses its stored value.

hypotheses.statement: The multiselect has no key and its options come in a different order on each rerun, so it gets a new identity and resets.
The selection is lost because the page is reloaded or reopened, which starts a new session.
The keyed widget is not rendered in some script run, so its state is cleaned up.
